deep.reconstruction:
Authorship and context. This page is not a Riemann derivation. It is a letter about Riemann's minimal-surface memoir "Über die Fläche vom kleinsten Inhalt bei gegebener Begrenzung", which K. Hattendorff edited ("Herr H."). The next page carries the date 18 Jan. 1876, the year the Werke appeared. The writer gives lectures in an "Auditoriengebäude", which suggests Göttingen. That fits H. A. Schwarz, writing to one of the Werke editors (Dedekind or Weber), but this attribution is my conjecture.

Opening paragraphs. The letter begins with personal matters: a photograph of a deceased person. The writer also declines to propose concrete rewordings for the passages he criticised.

The mathematical argument (after the afternoon lecture) concerns Article 14 of Hattendorff's text.
- Eq. 15 is a homogeneous linear 2nd-order ODE in the auxiliary variable t, with independent solutions K1, K2.
- Eq. 13 is a further 'linear differential equation' imposed on K1, K2. The order word is hard to read.

Step 1 (Abel's identity). For any two solutions of 15, the identity K1 dK2/dt − K2 dK1/dt = Const·dv/dt holds identically. Filled in by me: if 15 has the form K'' + p K' + q K = 0, then W' = −pW, so W = C·exp(−∫p dt). In Hattendorff's normalisation, exp(−∫p dt) is evidently dv/dt. So 13 can only constrain the multiplicative constant C carried by K1, K2.

Step 2 (the constant is inessential). Replacing v by c·v, or equivalently multiplying K1 and K2 by a common constant, changes C arbitrarily. The constant drops out of the ratio H = K2/K1. Therefore 13 can be dropped entirely.

Step 3 (general form of η). Instead one should simply set η = quotient of any two particular solutions of 15, i.e. η = (α K1 + β K2)/(γ K1 + δ K2) with complex α, β, γ, δ. Defined up to a common factor, this gives 3 complex = 6 real constants, whereas H. counts only 3.

Step 4 (next page; resolution of the count). Three of the six real constants correspond to a rotation of the sphere (H.'s α, α', θ). The other three correspond to the freedom of a real linear-fractional substitution for t, which preserves the real axis. That freedom can be used to make three of the boundary segments of the real t-axis correspond to great circles. Hence only C+E−3 conditions remain. This matches the previous page's point that the 2A+B+C+E parameters a, a', b, c, e amount to only 2A+B+C+E−3 constants.
errors: No mathematical error in the writer's argument; the Abel/Liouville Wronskian argument and the dimension count dim_R PSL(2,C) = 6 = 3 (SO(3) rotations) + 3 (PSL(2,R) reparametrisations of t) are correct as counts.

The 6 = 3 + 3 split is presented loosely as if the parameters split directly. It is really a dimension count (rotations plus normalisation via real Möbius maps of t), not a literal direct decomposition of PSL(2,C). This is acceptable as heuristic counting.

The writer criticises Hattendorff for undercounting constants: H. counts 3 for η where there are 6, and omits the −3 for the choice of t. Whether H.'s Eq. 16 truly restricts H is not verifiable from this page.

results.what: Wronskian of two solutions of the 2nd-order linear ODE (15) equals Const·dv/dt, so the auxiliary equation 13 only fixes an inessential multiplicative constant

The general quotient of two solutions is a Möbius transform (αK1+βK2)/(γK1+δK2) with 6 real parameters; 3 are rotations of the sphere and 3 are absorbed by real fractional-linear reparametrisation of t
results.modern_name: Projective (PSL(2,C)) ambiguity of the developing map / Schwarzian-type parameter count for Schwarz–Christoffel-like minimal-surface constructions

deep.surprise_reason: This is editorial correspondence (1876, probably Schwarz to a Werke editor) criticising Hattendorff's edition of Riemann's minimal-surface memoir. It is not original work by Riemann. The mathematics (Wronskian identity, Möbius parameter count) is routine, though the page is of historical interest for the editorial history of the Werke.
